audit_question.question: When F3 is established during recovery of an instance with prior accepted commands, can the matching prepare-reply threshold replace an already chosen value with NOOP and send that replacement for acceptance, or do supported execution configuration and initialization exclude this history?
audit_question.importance: Replacing an already chosen command sequence during recovery could allow different command sequences for one instance and inconsistent application effects. The source now establishes the replacement path and recovery entry, but a legal conflicting-decision execution has not been demonstrated.
participants: Replica whose application loop requests recovery
objects: Per-instance commands, promise ballot, value ballot and status
Configured read and write support sets
contexts: An existing accepted instance without local commit notification
Recovery bookkeeping with no client proposals
A matching prepare-reply threshold after recovery preparation
A supported configuration with intersecting distinct-participant support sets
event_paths: Prior acceptance -> delayed commit notification -> execution stalls -> recovery request is enqueued -> recover initializes missing bookkeeping and broadcasts Prepare -> PrepareReply carries retained commands and value ballot -> threshold replaces selected commands with NOOP -> bcastAccept sends the replacement
counterevidence: handlePrepare sends a full Commit instead of a PrepareReply when its local instance is COMMITTED; this can supply retained commands during recovery.
handleAccept preserves an existing COMMITTED instance and rejects lower-ballot mutation. These guards do not themselves protect replicas that accepted a value but have not learned its commitment.
handlePrepareReply rejects lower-ballot replies and routes higher-ballot replies through the nack branch; the selected replacement requires matching replies.

Fresh handlePropose admission increments crtInstance; it does not by itself establish reuse of a previously accepted instance. The immediate investigation therefore follows recovery with absent client proposals.

ReadQuorumSize returns N-F and WriteQuorumSize returns F+1. Their sum is N+1, but set intersection requires valid membership parameters and distinct participants; counters alone do not establish those premises.
F3 remains a local assignment fact. Neither prior acceptance alone nor the threshold counter establishes that a value was already chosen.
Actual delivery, ordering and supported execution activation remain unverified; source-level sends and recovery enqueue operations do not establish completed handoffs.
unknowns: Which constructor/run configuration starts executeCommands and enables the observed recovery path.
Exact Instance and LeaderBookkeeping field declarations and initial replica ballot values needed to construct a legal bounded history.
How N, F and participant identities are initialized and which concrete intersecting-support configuration is supported.
Whether a fully correlated legal history can establish prior choice, delay relevant commit notifications, and obtain matching preparation replies before a protective full Commit is processed.
Whether subsequent replacement acceptance can produce a conflicting decision under actual transport and scheduling semantics.
The client-proposal replacement variant remains outside the immediate recovery discriminator and is not explained by narrowing to NOOP.
Durable restart semantics are not established; the immediate candidate concerns retained in-memory acceptance and delayed messages.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The new source resolves several earlier gaps: handleAccept installs commands and vbal; handlePrepare reports those fields for noncommitted instances; recover preserves an existing instance and creates bookkeeping without client proposals when missing; executeCommands enqueues recovery after a stalled prefix. makeBallot only assigns lastTriedBallot and does not reset counters or adopt retained commands. The threshold subsequently replaces lb.cmds with NOOP and bcastAccept propagates it. Committed-state protections are real but local, leaving an accepted-without-commit-notification history as the decisive case. Startup activation and membership initialization are the next bounded prerequisites.

input.selection_rationale: Continue the same F3 establishment candidate. Source review establishes a concrete recovery path capable of reaching the NOOP branch and narrows the protection question to replicas that retain acceptance without local commitment. This is progress beyond observing an assignment overwrite, but does not establish prior choice, supported configuration, or a conflicting decision. Read the exact startup and membership initialization ranges before attributing a value-preservation obligation. The supplied inventory already distinguishes recovery enqueue and recovery entry, and outbound-consumer enrichment is already pending; no additional descriptive correction is justified here.

question.question: When F3 is established by a matching prepare-reply threshold, can a legal later attempt replace previously accepted commands with client-proposal commands or NOOP despite preparation reporting those commands, or do the reply producer, attempt initialization, quorum configuration, or committed-instance handling exclude the consequential history?
question.importance: The threshold-selected commands are passed directly into outgoing Accept messages. If a legal later attempt can replace an already decided value and obtain sufficient acceptance, replicas could apply different operations for one instance. The current source establishes replacement and propagation, but not that consequential execution.
contexts: An instance with possible prior accepted commands
A later preparation attempt reaching the local reply threshold
Client-proposal and NOOP selection branches
event_paths: Earlier acceptance -> later preparation -> matching reply records commands by VBallot -> threshold overwrites lb.cmds -> bcastAccept sends overwritten commands
counterevidence: handlePrepareReply rejects replies below lastTriedBallot and routes higher-ballot replies through a nack branch; the observed overwrite requires matching ballots.
handlePropose increments crtInstance before initializing a proposal instance, so ordinary fresh proposal admission alone does not establish reuse of an earlier accepted instance.
handlePropose can bypass preparation when lastTriedBallot equals smallestDefaultBallot; the selected suspicion concerns the preparation threshold path.
F3 describes a local assignment, not a quorum-backed selected-value guarantee. An applicable requirement still needs the producer and legal-history analysis.
Committed-instance response and mutation protections remain navigation-based possibilities until their exact source is attached.
unknowns: Whether PrepareReply.Command and VBallot represent prior acceptance in the relevant legal history, including empty commands and initialization sentinels.
How ballot construction initializes or resets counters, selected value ballots, and local self-support.
Whether recovery or retry can prepare an instance with prior acceptance while clientProposals is absent or contains different commands.
Whether committed-instance handling prevents the relevant later selection or acceptance, including histories where acceptance occurred without commit notification.
Which configured read and write thresholds and participant assumptions justify an intersecting-support value-preservation requirement.
question.trigger_rationale: The attached handler first records commands from a greater VBallot, then unconditionally replaces lb.cmds with client commands or NOOP at the threshold. The attached bcastAccept reads that same lb.cmds without further value selection. This resolves the immediate overwrite and downstream-use discriminator; producer semantics and legal prior-acceptance histories remain decisive.

history.question: When the prepare-reply threshold establishes F3 for an instance and attempt, how does the handler choose between previously accepted commands reported during preparation and its client-proposal commands or NOOP? Does the actual path retain and use the relevant accepted-value information, or is that responsibility supplied by another mechanism?
history.importance: Value selection during a new attempt can affect whether an instance retains a previously decided operation. An incompatible selection could lead to divergent replicated state if later accepted and applied. The applicability of that consequence depends on the actual preparation and selection mechanisms and is not established by the inventory.
contexts: An instance with possible prior accepted commands
A preparation attempt reaching the local reply threshold
Client-proposal and NOOP selection branches
event_paths: Prepare processing -> reply collection -> threshold value assignment -> accept propagation
counterevidence: The inventory describes matching prepare replies and a per-attempt lastTriedBallot; these may constrain stale replies, but their implementation and sufficiency remain unread.
F3 explicitly establishes only a local assignment, not a selected-value guarantee. Its descriptive meaning alone does not justify a consensus obligation.
unknowns: Which accepted-value and ballot information preparation replies convey.
How reply processing retains, compares, and selects reported commands.
Whether client-proposal or NOOP assignment is conditional on the absence of relevant previously accepted commands.
Whether another branch or mechanism supplies the value-selection responsibility.
Which legal attempt histories and participant assumptions make a value-preservation requirement applicable.
history.trigger_rationale: The provisional inventory places client-proposal or NOOP assignment at a prepare-reply threshold. Comparing the reply producer with that consumer offers a bounded discriminator for F3 establishment without assuming that the assignment is defective.
